newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania average auctioned rate dives to 226.31 pct.
newsitem.headline: Romania average auctioned rate dives to 226.31 pct.

text.p: The average one-week rate of Romania's central bank (BNR) auctioned funds dived on Thursday to 226.31 percent from an all-time high of 426.50 percent last week due to undersubscription on a balanced money market.

At Thursday's refinancing auction the BNR had raised its offer to 660 billion lei from 510 billion, with five commercial banks bidding only 650 billion lei, at rates between 226 percent and 230 percent, as the money market turned liquid.

The BNR also set the minimum permitted rate to 226 percent, although it had previously said that rate would be set by the market at the weekly auctions. On Thursday, the valid minimum rate should have been around 426 percent.

BNR officials said Thursday's slash in the minimum rate was decided because last week's high average rate had reflected seasonal factors linked with the end of the month when most banks chase for leu funds to meet their reserve targets.

Money market operators said most inter-bank prices, which traded at about 446 percent on Thursday, were expected to follow the fall in the average rate. They said leu shortages narrowed due to fresh leu inflows on the money market.
The Lombard rate, applied to overdraft credits and set by multiplying the average auctioned rate by 1.6, is also expected to fall from the current all-time high of 682.4 percent.
